title: Processing full chunks of symbols
statement: Let $\sigma$ and $\alpha$ be types, let $w$ be a natural number, let $\delta$ assign an element of $\sigma$ to each element of $\sigma$ and each finite list of elements of $\alpha$, and let $s\in\sigma$. Suppose $L$ is a finite list of finite lists of elements of $\alpha$, each of length $w+1$, and let the initial buffer assign an element of $\alpha$ to each of the $w+1$ positions. Processing the concatenation of the lists in $L$ one symbol at a time, updating the state by $\delta$ whenever a full block of $w+1$ symbols has been processed, ends with state equal to the result of applying $\delta$ successively to the lists in $L$, starting from $s$, and with position zero, for some final buffer.
hypotheses_covered: $\delta$ maps a state and a finite list of symbols to a state
$L$ is a finite list of finite lists of symbols
The initial buffer assigns a symbol to each of the $w+1$ positions
